newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean won ends down on stronger dlr/yen.
newsitem.headline: South Korean won ends down on stronger dlr/yen.

text.p: The won finished lower versus the dollar on Monday pressured by large import deals and the dollar's strength against the Japanese yen in world markets, traders said.
Some long dollar holders squared their positions in the afternoon, but failed to erase losses in early trading, they said.
The won closed at 893.10, compared with Friday's close of 892.70. It traded in a range of 893.00 to 896.50.
Traders said the won started weak early in the session in line with the dollar's rise against the yen.
However, the fall was halted as rumours that the central bank would stand firm behind the won spread.
"The sentiment turned bearish in the afternoon and longs started selling," said a foreign bank dealer.
Traders expect Tuesday's trading to depend heavily on the dollar/yen movement.
"The dollar could shoot up to 900 if the dollar/yen soars," said the foreign bank dealer.
A wide range of 892.50 to 900 is seen for Tuesday.
